record.paper_title: Orthogonal polynomials and approximation theory: some open problems
record.original_question: Let D be a domain and let f be a function. Suppose that every diagonal Padé approximant to f is holomorphic in D. Must f itself be holomorphic in D, or can one construct a counterexample?

evidence.quote: Prove (or give a counterexample): If all diagonal Padé approximants to f are holomorphic in D, then f is holomorphic in D.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $D \subseteq \mathbb{C}$ be a domain and let $f$ be a formal power series (say, centered at a point of $D$) regarded as a function. For each pair of nonnegative integers $(n,n)$, let $[n/n]_f$ denote the diagonal Padé approximant of $f$, i.e. the rational function $P_n/Q_n$ with $\deg P_n \le n$, $\deg Q_n \le n$, $Q_n \not\equiv 0$, satisfying $Q_n(z) f(z) - P_n(z) = O(z^{2n+1})$ at the center of expansion. Suppose that for every $n \ge 0$ the diagonal Padé approximant $[n/n]_f$ is holomorphic in all of $D$ (i.e. has no poles in $D$). 

Prove that $f$ admits a holomorphic continuation to $D$, or construct a counterexample: a function $f$ all of whose diagonal Padé approximants are holomorphic in $D$ but which itself does not extend holomorphically to $D$.
artifact.status_search_result: A targeted web search did not yield a definitive resolution of this specific question. The surrounding theory (Nuttall–Stahl theory on convergence of diagonal Padé approximants, and the fact that uniform holomorphy of the diagonal sequence in a domain forces convergence there) is well developed, but no source explicitly confirms a proof or counterexample to the stated implication. The status is therefore reported as unknown.

status_evidence.title: Padé approximants for functions with branch points — strong asymptotics of Nuttall–Stahl polynomials
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses Nuttall–Stahl theory on the convergence of diagonal Padé approximants and their relation to the analytic continuation of f.
status_evidence.claim: The convergence theory of diagonal Padé approximants is closely tied to the holomorphy domain of f, but does not directly settle the converse implication considered here.

status_evidence.title: Diagonal Padé Approximants — overview
status_evidence.snippet: Overview of diagonal Padé approximants noting that holomorphy of approximants in a domain implies their uniform convergence inside.
status_evidence.claim: Standard references discuss holomorphy and convergence of diagonal Padé approximants but do not explicitly resolve the stated converse problem.
